residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD — no trade recorded, in the south division, where it is counted after the re-family recorded above; it was drawn in the west division. NOBODY HERE IS NAMED BY ANY SOURCE. The 1840 Chicago schedule counts children under ten at 27% of the town and women of twenty to twenty-nine as its second-largest band; the 1835 layer the sources can name holds 15 women, because the rolls that name this town — a letter list, a voters' roll, a subscription — print men. That gap is the shape of the evidence and not a reading of the town, so the order book counts it bucket by bucket and this household is drawn against those counts. Every value on it carries the model row and the seed that redraws it, and a source naming a woman who kept her own house in this division retires the whole record. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). This household is one of the surplus the re-cut HOLDS rather than retires: the owner's ruling of 2026-09-24 re-families it into a cell the book still orders instead of un-writing it, and `refamilied` above is the whole of what that changed.

persons.name: Joseph Skinner
persons.note: THE LADDER'S OWN READING OF THIS EVIDENCE. Read from newspaper_letter_list, tax_1833. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. tax_1833 stands against this person's name by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. THE 1833 TAX LIST IS A PROPERTY ROLL, NOT A RESIDENCE CHECK (T-1117): it names the owner of ground inside the town, resident or not, and its own entry 110 is a man three years dead. It bounds the town's RECORD of this name and not the day this person reached Chicago. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the town's own paper carries this name by 1 July 1835; whether the man it names was standing in the town is a claim this record cannot make, and present_on_scene_date says `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Skinner, Joseph” (tax_1833_095, line 147). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Skinner' agrees with the entry's forenames; 3 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Skinner, John B. | Profession. | January 12, 1S77.” (second_presb_0311, printed page 171), admitted by profession, the roll not printing when. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Skinner' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins J. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). The sources stop short of 1 July 1835 for this household and nothing puts it anywhere else; the town's rule (T-1386) counts it present, and no source says where it slept. The roof is the invention and the people are not.

persons.name: Samuel E. Toby
persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G3, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN PRINTED THREE TIMES. The return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office on 1 July 1834 was set three times in the Chicago Democrat — 1834-07-02 p3 c2, 1834-07-09 p1 c2 and 1834-07-16 p1 c2 — and two of those settings print 'samuel E. Toby' where the middle one prints 'samuel. Toby' and sets no middle initial at all. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-09-24 (T-1528) that a present initial may absorb an ABSENT one at the same entry of the same list, bounded exactly as T-0392's unread-initial ruling was, and the gazetteer now keys this person on 'Samuel E. Toby' — the reading that carries every letter a printing set, which tools/compile_gazetteer.py refuses to let a merge discard. THIS CARD WEARS THAT READING (T-1561). It displayed 'Samuel. Toby' until then, which is the ABSORBED side: after the merge, nothing this record cites read the name that way, and the surviving reading was sitting in this card's own press_evidence row. THE ID DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE NAME — `toby_samuel` is a handle every crosswalk cites and not a claim (rule N5, T-1139), and the family name it was minted off is the one the card still reads. AND THE FIELD NOW FOLLOWS THE MERGED RECORD (T-1562). `letter_list_returns` is one date PER RETURN and not per printing, so three impressions of the 1 July 1834 return put ONE date in it, and it is the first printing that carries the name: 1834-07-02. It held the 1834-07-09 impression until then, which was neither the first printing nor the last but the issue one extraction crop reached. Reading the last printing in instead would date the evidence by a compositor's re-run; carrying both ends would say the office held letters for this man in two separate returns, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is not what happened. THE ARRIVAL BLOCK DID NOT MOVE — it is dated by the return and never by the impression (T-0425), so it read 1834-07-01 while the earliest printing behind the name was still eight days late, and it reads 1834-07-01 now. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
